title: Pan Dulce with Raisins and Icing

content.title: About
content.content: Pan Dulce is a traditional Mexican sweet bread, soft and fragrant, often enriched with raisins and topped with a sweet icing. The dough is made from wheat flour, eggs, butter, sugar and yeast, then raisins are folded in, adding a subtle fruity note. After baking, the loaf is glazed with a sugar icing, creating a pleasant contrast between the tender crumb and the crisp sweet crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pan Dulce originated in colonial Mexico, where Spanish pastry chefs adapted European recipes to local ingredients.
It is traditionally served during holidays, especially Day of the Dead and Christmas.
Raisins not only add sweetness but also retain moisture, keeping the bread soft and fresh longer.
Icing is usually made from powdered sugar, milk and vanilla, though some regions use honey or caramel syrup.
There are many regional variations: in Yucatán orange zest is added, while in Oaxaca pecans are common.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates and modest fat content provide a quick source of energy.

items.title: Rich in raisins
items.content: Raisins supply iron, potassium and antioxidants that support hemoglobin levels and cell protection.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough contributes B1, B2 and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Butter and milk in the recipe help strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Raisins and whole‑grain flour (when used) add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The icing and raisins make the product sweet, which can be problematic for people with diabetes or those limiting sugar.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, so it is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of butter, sugar and raisins, Pan Dulce is relatively high in calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Dried fruit sensitivity
items.content: Raisins may cause increased gas in individuals with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pan Dulce is enjoyed as a dessert with tea or coffee, sliced and lightly warmed. It pairs well with hot chocolate, fruit sauces, or cream cheese spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate (up to 1 week) or freeze (up to 2 months). Allow the bread to come to room temperature before serving.
